title: Scion — microfeature seeding notebook
content:
Brief: jotting down a lightweight pattern for shipping very small, tightly scoped features ("scions") into the hosted product to learn adoption and ops cost before committing to a full productization cycle. Idea is intentionally cheap: minimal UI, opt-in via query param / flag, short TTL, telemetry first.

Why? Observations: large PRDs slow us down; we often want to test demand and cost implications (tokens, latency, SLO impact) quickly. Existing "microfeature" ideas tend to balloon into design/ops work. Scion = a grafted experiment that can be grown or pruned depending on signals.

High-level goals:
- Validate user value for a narrowly scoped behavior in 2–6 weeks.
- Measure end-to-end cost (per-request token delta, backend CPU/GPU impact, latency delta).
- Capture qualitative feedback with minimal UX.
- Ensure safe rollback with automated pruning.

Core constraints (must-have for any scion):
- Feature toggled by: client SDK flag + server-side feature key.
- Short-lived model pin allowed (e.g., llama-2-small or q4_kv) to bound cost.
- Default: opt-out for existing customers; opt-in via a query param ?scion=<id> or SDK flag.
- Telemetry: event for scion_invoked, scion_cost_tokens, scion_latency_ms, scion_fallback.
- Pruning: TTL auto-disable after X days of low usage OR high cost signal.

Example scion candidates (seed ideas):
1) Compact Recap (very short summary appended to chat threads to help re-entry).
   - 2–3 templated sentences, generated at low temp, pinned to small model.
   - User story: As a user returning to a conversation, I want a 1-2 line recap so I can jump back in.
   - Hypothesis: increases session resumption rate and reduces token churn when users ask for context.
2) Quick Fact-Check (on-demand small rerank against cached sources).
   - Runs a lightweight classifier + embedding similarity, limited to top 3 docs.
   - User story: As a user, I want a short verification of a claim instead of a long search.
3) Inline Style Tone (single-line tone modifier presets: concise/polite/technical).
   - Quick toggle that prepends a short system instruction.
   - Aim: productize later if we see preference signals.

Acceptance metrics (primary):
- Engagement: % of sessions that use scion when shown (or opted-in) within test cohort.
- Value proxy: fraction of users who mark it "helpful" (simple emoji) or do follow-up prompt that indicates relevance.
- Cost: delta tokens per session and 95th percentile latency difference.
- Reliability: fallback rate to base model.

Instrumentation checklist (minimal):
- Add scion_id tag to all spans/traces and to logs.
- Emit scion_cost_tokens metric (sum & p50/p95).
- Counter for scion_disabled_auto_prune events.

Rollout plan (fast):
- Day 0–3: internal beta (10 engineers) via SDK flag.
- Day 4–14: opt-in beta for selected customers (customer success list), server-side gating.
- Day 15–30: A/B small cohort (2% of users) vs control; monitor cost/latency and NPS micro-feedback.
- Decision gates at day 30: grow to productization or prune.

Quick API sketch (proto):
- Request header: X-Scion-ID: recap_v1
- SDK: client.scion.enable('recap_v1')
- Server: /v1/generate body includes {scion_id: "recap_v1", scion_model_hint: "small", scion_ttl_days: 21}

Edge cases / risks:
- Hidden cost blowup if scion prompts cascade (e.g., user asks follow-ups that multiply tokens).
  - Mitigation: token budget per scion invocation; hard cap per session.
- Privacy: some scions might surface sensitive data. Need quick safety review checklist for any scion.
- Observability: if we do many scions, telemetry must scale and be easy to query.

To-dos (short):
- [ ] Draft standard scion safety checklist (Lena)
- [ ] Wire minimal telemetry schema in events (Devon)
- [ ] Prototype SDK flag + header flow (me)
- [ ] Pick first scion to try (vote: Compact Recap)
- [ ] Setup quick Confluence playbook for running a scion test (template with metrics)

Open questions:
- What is the right TTL default? 21 days feels right but maybe 14 is better for rapid pruning.
- Do we force scion model family (small) or allow a budgeted scatter across model tiers?
- Where do scion experiments live in product roadmap repo? Under experiments/ or feature-prototypes/?

Notes to self:
- Keep UX minimal: a single subtle UI affordance (toggle in settings or inline pill) + small feedback control (thumbs up/down).
- Make sure rollback is one-click at infra level: feature flag off + quick delete of model pins.
- Can we reuse existing prefix cache? Many scions will be prefix-based (recaps); reuse reduces cost.

Mini next-steps (this week):
- Prototype header + minimal server flow -> smoke test with local model to measure token delta.
- Run quick estimate: if scion adds 40 tokens on average and 5% of sessions use it, what's monthly cost impact for 10k DAU? (back-of-envelope: 10k * 0.05 * 40 tokens * price-per-token)

Related refs:
- prototype: github.com/redwood-inference/prototypes/recap-draft
- earlier notes: local-notebook: compact-recap-ideas (internal)

End.
(Keeping this as my rough single-file brain-dump. Will split into tidy PRD if Compact Recap gets greenlit.)
